structured.approach: I followed the DE-06 procedure in the data-engineering-steps skill, which reads feat.data_model_change and org.customer_mappings and writes feat.mappings. I read both contracted inputs, the shared memory and journey board, and the ap_pipeline tool view. I also read data/sample_feed.csv from the checkout to see which feed version the repository exercises. I compared the vendor's v3 contract with the DE-05 model change item by item: version, columns, spelling, format, target and schedule. Then I wrote the source-to-target mapping, the processing order for each row, the derived late-payment history mapping, the schedule check and test cases for DE-08/DE-09. The output describes only what the inputs, the tool view and the cited repository file hold. It makes no statement about CI or git results, because no cited source holds them. The mapping is implemented in DE-08, so no code changed. I used no connectors, because the inputs held everything needed.

claims.text: The vendor feed v3 columns are invoice_id, vendor, due_date, amount, paid and paid_date. paid_date is optional, an ISO date, and empty when unpaid. The mapping is paid_date -> Invoice.paid_date.
The customer schedule is daily 02:00 Asia/Kolkata, unchanged. It matches schedule.json (frequency daily, time 02:00, timezone Asia/Kolkata), so no schedule change is needed.
The registered Invoice entity already holds paid_date (date or None). The existing fields id, vendor, due_date, amount and paid keep their mappings and types.

paid_date maps to None when it is missing, None, blank or whitespace only. Otherwise it is date.fromisoformat(value.strip()). A non-blank invalid value rejects the row with reason paid_date (constant PAID_DATE_REASON). An existing reject reason wins because paid_date is validated last (DD-6).
The data-quality report needs no code change. reject_reasons is the sorted set of rejected reasons, so paid_date appears in it automatically.

The Delay history is Dict[str, List[int]] keyed by vendor. delay_days = (paid_date - due_date).days, for paid records with a paid_date only, in feed order and in memory only. ap_forecast vendor_risk consumes it.
amount stays Decimal and is never float.
The repository sample feed has only the v2 header (invoice_id,vendor,due_date,amount,paid), so v3 test cases need synthetic rows.
The tool view shows transform.py without paid_date and no delays.py module. IN-3 and IN-7 implement the mapping in DE-08 Coding.
The customer contract confirms the spelling paid_date, which answers the open question DMQ-2 (carried CQ-I1) in the data model change.

open_questions: MQ-1: The customer contract lists the column as paid_date. Can DMQ-2 (carried CQ-I1, spelling) be closed? Interim: yes.

MQ-2: The customer contract says paid_date is 'empty when unpaid', while the model's interim rule DD-7 (DMQ-3) keeps a valid paid_date on an unpaid record. Should such a row be rejected, or its paid_date cleared, instead? Interim: keep it; the Delay history ignores it.
MQ-3: The customer contract names only 'v3' and gives no effective date. Must v2 and v3 feeds be accepted side by side for a period? Interim: yes; the mapping already accepts both.
MQ-4 (carried DMQ-1): Should org.data_model register the paid_date reject reason and the Delay history structure org-wide?
structured.summary: I wrote feat.mappings for DE-06. The vendor's latest mapping (feed v3) adds one mapping, paid_date -> Invoice.paid_date (nullable date; a non-blank invalid value rejects the row with reason paid_date). The existing column mappings are unchanged, and the mapping agrees with the DE-05 data model change field by field. The document gives the processing steps for each row in order, the derived Invoice-to-late-payment-history mapping, a schedule check (daily 02:00 Asia/Kolkata matches schedule.json, no change) and test cases for DE-08/DE-09. This step changes no code. There are four non-blocking open questions; MQ-2 is a wording difference between the contract's 'empty when unpaid' and the model's interim DD-7 rule.
